questions.prompt:
At an air temperature of \(32^\circ\mathrm F\), the wind chill, in degrees Fahrenheit, is modelled by
\[
W(v)=55.6-22.1v^{0.16},
\]
where \(v\) is the wind velocity in miles per hour and \(5\le v\le60\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find \(W'(20)\). Using correct units, explain its meaning in terms of wind chill.
parts.answer:
\[
W'(v)=-3.536v^{-0.84},
\qquad
\boxed{W'(20)\approx-0.286\ ^\circ\mathrm F/\mathrm{mph}}.
\]
At a wind velocity of \(20\) mph, the perceived wind chill decreases by approximately \(0.286^\circ\mathrm F\) for each additional mile per hour of wind speed.

parts.label: (c)

parts.answer:
At \(t=3\), \(v=20+5(3)=35\) mph. By the chain rule,
\[
\frac{dW}{dt}=W'(v)\frac{dv}{dt}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{\frac{dW}{dt}=W'(35)(5)\approx-0.892\ ^\circ\mathrm F/\mathrm{hour}}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Consider the closed curve in the \(xy\)-plane given by
\[
x^2+2x+y^4+4y=5.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Show that
\[
\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{x+1}{2(y^3+1)}.
\]
parts.answer:
Differentiating implicitly,
\[
2x+2+(4y^3+4)\frac{dy}{dx}=0.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{x+1}{2(y^3+1)}}.
\]

parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the two points on the curve where the tangent is vertical.
parts.answer:
A vertical tangent occurs when \(2(y^3+1)=0\), so \(y=-1\). Substitution into the curve gives

questions.prompt: A continuous function \(f\) on \([-4,6]\) consists of a line segment for \(-4\le x\le0\) and a twice-differentiable curve for \(0<x<6\), tangent to the \(x\)-axis at \(x=3\), with \(f''(x)>0\) on \((0,6)\), as shown in the supplied graph.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Is \(f\) differentiable at \(x=0\)? Use one-sided difference quotients.
parts.answer:
The left-hand derivative equals the line-segment slope,
\[
\lim_{h\to0^-}\frac{f(h)-f(0)}h=\frac23.
\]
The right-hand derivative is negative from the source graph. Since the one-sided derivatives are unequal, \(\boxed{f\text{ is not differentiable at }x=0}\).

The derivative of \(f\) is
\[
f'(x)=\begin{cases}
g(x),&-4\le x\le0,\\
5e^{-x/3}-3,&0<x\le4,
\end{cases}

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: For \(-4<x<4\), find all inflection-point \(x\)-coordinates of \(f\).

Inflection points occur where \(f'\) changes monotonicity. The semicircle changes from decreasing to increasing at \(x=-2\), and at \(x=0\) the derivative changes from increasing to decreasing. Thus
\[
\boxed{x=-2\text{ and }x=0}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Snow accumulates on Janet's driveway from midnight to 9 a.m. at rate
\[
f(t)=7te^{\cos t}
\]
cubic feet per hour, where \(t\) is hours after midnight. Janet removes snow at rate
\[
g(t)=\begin{cases}
0,&0\le t<6,\\
125,&6\le t<7,\\
108,&7\le t\le9.
\end{cases}
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: How many cubic feet of snow have accumulated by 6 a.m.?
parts.answer:
\[
\boxed{\int_0^6 7te^{\cos t}\,dt\approx142.275\ \text{ft}^3}.
\]

\]

Using signed areas under \(g'\),

g(3)=5+\pi+\frac32=\boxed{\frac{13}{2}+\pi},

g(-2)=5-\pi=\boxed{5-\pi}.
\]

parts.prompt: Let \(h(x)=g(x)-\frac12x^2\). Find and classify every critical point of \(h\) for \(-7<x<5\).
parts.answer:
\[
h'(x)=g'(x)-x.
\]
On the semicircle, \(\sqrt{4-x^2}=x\) gives \(x=\sqrt2\). The line segments also give \(x=3\). The derivative changes from positive to negative at \(\sqrt2\), but remains negative on both sides of \(3\). Hence
\[
\boxed{x=\sqrt2\text{ is a relative maximum};\qquad x=3\text{ is neither}}.
\]
